raw_response:
I have been farming these fields for 35 years, since I was 15 years old. I finished middle school here in Quzhou, and everything I know about cotton I learned by doing it, by watching my father, and by copying the neighbors who get good harvests. My farm is 13.1 mu, and cotton is the only crop I grow on it. My household has six people — my husband and my eldest son work off-farm in construction in Handan, so they send cash home. That helps with school fees for my grandson, but the cotton is still what keeps this family fed and clothed. I cannot afford a bad year.

Last season I got about 250 kg of seed cotton per mu. That was decent, but Lao Zhang on the east side of the village got 280 kg because he did not cut back on fertilizer when prices went up. I watched his field — the bolls were bigger and the plants stayed green longer. This year I will do what he did.

I will buy improved insect-resistant cotton seeds from the input dealer in town. I pay about 60 yuan per mu for them. I do not save my own seeds anymore — the bought ones grow stronger and I spray less for bollworm.

In late March I will run the rotary tiller over the whole field to break up the soil. Before planting in late April, I will spread 40 kg of compound fertilizer per mu as my base — the bag says 15-15-15, so that is 6 kg of nitrogen, 6 kg of phosphorus, and 6 kg of potassium right there. When the cotton starts flowering in early July, I will topdress with 25 kg of urea per mu — that is another 11.5 kg of nitrogen. I will also spread 5 kg of potassium chloride per mu because cotton needs extra potassium when the bolls are forming, and last August my plants looked yellow and weak on the edges. In total that comes to about 17.5 kg of nitrogen, 6 kg of phosphorus, and 9 kg of potassium per mu. I know this fertilizer will cost me more than 300 yuan per mu, but I would rather waste some fertilizer than lose yield. If the harvest fails, I have to borrow money from my brother-in-law, and I hate that.

I irrigate four times from my well: once right after planting to help the seeds sprout, once at early flowering, once at peak flowering in mid-July, and once when the bolls are filling in late August. My well has enough water for 13 mu if I pump at night when the electricity is cheaper.

For pesticides, even with the Bt cotton, I spray three times: once for aphids when the weather turns hot in June, once for spider mites in August, and once more in late August if I see any worms or leaf spots. Each spray costs me about 40 yuan per mu for the chemicals and my time mixing.

At picking time I hire two women from the village because my waist cannot handle bending all day anymore. I pay them by the jin they pick.

If the weather is normal — not like the drought two years ago — I expect to harvest about 260 kg of seed cotton per mu this year.
